name: Cassava Green Mite
description: A destructive spider mite that feeds on cassava leaves, causing chlorotic spots and defoliation. It was accidentally introduced to Africa from South America and is now a major pest in cassava-growing regions.
symptoms: Yellowish chlorotic spots on young leaves
Premature leaf drop starting from top of plant
Stunted growth and reduced root yield
treatments: Apply sulfur-based acaricides (not during hot weather)
Use neem oil or insecticidal soap every 5-7 days
Introduce predatory mites (Typhlodromalus aripo, T. manihoti) as biocontrol
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies
prevention: Conserve and introduce predatory mites from IITA biological control program
Maintain soil moisture to reduce mite stress on plants
Monitor young leaves regularly for early detection
